label: JZ Mock A · Paper 2 · Question 12
knowledgePattern: Respect both branches of a variable-base logarithmic graph
solution:
Changing base gives y=log24/log2(x−1)=2/log2(x−1). For 1<x<2 the denominator is negative, while for x>2 it is positive. Thus I is false.

The function decreases on each separate branch, but not on the whole disconnected domain. For instance 3/2<3, whereas y(3/2)=−2<2=y(3). This contradicts the required inequality for a strictly decreasing function, so II is false.

No allowed base raised to the power zero equals 4, so the value y=0 is never attained. III is false. As x tends to infinity, log2(x−1) grows without bound and y tends to zero. Hence IV is true. Answer D.

hints.title: Fix the base in a new representation
hints.body: Use change of base to express the function as a constant divided by a logarithm with a fixed valid base.
hints.recap: Logarithms represent exponents; their arguments must be positive and their bases positive and different from one.
hints.pitfall: The base here varies with x; do not sketch an ordinary fixed-base logarithm directly.
hints.pause: Find the signs and excluded input in your new expression.

hints.title: Test the whole stated domain
hints.body: Test monotonicity using one point from each side of the missing input, then examine whether every proposed output can occur.
hints.recap: A reciprocal graph has separated branches; decreasing on each branch need not mean decreasing across their union.
hints.pitfall: A missing value between two branches must not be filled in.
hints.pause: Check the first three claims with allowed values or range reasoning.

hints.title: Look at the far end
hints.body: Consider how the fixed-base logarithm in your denominator behaves for very large x.
hints.recap: A fixed-base logarithm with base greater than one increases without bound as its positive input increases without bound.
hints.pitfall: An asymptote may be approached without ever being attained.
hints.pause: Determine the limiting height and classify the remaining claim.
